clue.text: Habitat for game beginning to grow naturally around lake

indicators.note: the beginning of the word grow is its opening letter
the phrase for naturally goes around the letter for lake

parts.note: naturally, as in 'of course', 'needless to say'
L is the usual abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Somewhere wild game animals might live, growing naturally around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' sounds like wild animals, but it is the game of golf. 'around' puts L inside OF COURSE after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a game, and the place it is played, its home ground, can be called its habitat.

clue.text: My hotel's introduced an element of Asian cuisine

indicators.note: the hotel letter is introduced into the exclamation, placed within it

parts.note: 'My!' and 'Gee!' are both exclamations of surprise
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel restaurant boasts that it has added an Asian ingredient to its menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation GEE; 'introduced' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarified butter is a staple ingredient of Indian and South Asian cooking.

clue.text: With title cut, movie to get reworked theme music?

indicators.note: reworked means the letters are rearranged into a new order
a word that is cut loses its tail, so the final letter of title goes

explanation.surface: A film retitled and re-edited, with its theme music reworked too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims TITLE to TITL; 'reworked' shuffles TITL and MOVIE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring musical phrase tied to a character or idea, as in Wagner's operas, is a theme; the question mark admits it is a loose gloss.

clue.text: Jump over net

definitions.meaning: to leap over a fence or bar without touching it
to earn as profit after deductions, as in taking home a sum

explanation.surface: A tennis or volleyball instruction to leap the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a high jumper gets over the bar, and a business makes so much after costs.

clue.text: By the middle of June, husband has yearning for divorce, perhaps

indicators.note: the middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy and crosswords
an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: A spouse feels the urge for a divorce by midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of JUNE is UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach two things once joined; a divorce, by example, is the undoing of a marriage, getting hitched in reverse.

clue.text: Sickly in hospital? On the contrary, it's superficial

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed within another
reverses the stated relation: the hospital goes in the sickly word, not the other way round

parts.note: sallow means of an unhealthy yellowish complexion
H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs and maps

explanation.surface: A patient looks sickly in hospital, or so it seems on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue first suggests SALLOW in H; 'On the contrary' swaps that, so H goes into SALLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean lacking depth, whether of water or of thought and feeling: straight synonyms.

clue.text: Book features a chapter on Eliot

parts.note: T.S. Eliot, the poet, known by his initials

explanation.surface: A book has a chapter devoted to the poet Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot gives his initials TS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament, often called simply by its short name.

clue.text: A hundred years, approximately, before the French Revolution

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
c. stands for circa, Latin for about
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Roughly a century passed before the French Revolution of 1789.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French Revolution' looks like one historical event, but 'the French' gives LE and 'Revolution' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: One complete turn round a circuit, as of a wheel or pedal, is a revolution.

clue.text: Dearest wife gets covered in foam when visiting works

indicators.note: visiting puts one piece next to the other, calling on it
the wife letter is covered by the word for foam, placed inside it

parts.note: to seethe is to foam or froth, as boiling water does
works of art, as in a gallery

explanation.surface: A wife gets drenched in froth during a tour of some factory works.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a loved one; 'Dearest' is used the same way in addressing a partner.

clue.text: Switching letter in online Scrabble? It's for the best

indicators.note: two letters swap places, turning a stretch of the online piece back to front

parts.note: E- is the prefix for electronic or online things
a letter tile is the piece used in the board game Scrabble

explanation.surface: A tip for winning at online Scrabble: switch a letter for best effect.
explanation.walkthrough: An online Scrabble piece would be an E-TILE; swapping the T and L in it (reversing TIL to LIT) gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group, its top people, are the best of it: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Discover facial hair and get upset

parts.note: to hear is to find out or learn of news
tache is short for moustache

explanation.surface: Someone finds an unwanted moustache growing and is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief or distress is an upset, the noun sense, as when a loss causes sorrow.

clue.text: Sports administrators tucked into endless snacks and pudding

indicators.note: one piece is tucked inside another
endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: tapas are Spanish snack dishes
the IOC is the International Olympic Committee

explanation.surface: Olympic officials tucking into snacks and a dessert at a reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like eating, but it puts IOC inside TAPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca, made from cassava starch, is cooked with milk as a classic British school dessert.

clue.text: In backing strike, write unrestricted article relating to union matters

indicators.note: in signals that the following pieces go within the reversed strike word
backing means read in reverse

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit

indicators.note: with its limits, the first and last letters, removed

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A trade unionist writes a piece supporting a strike, all about union matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests trade unions but means marriage. 'backing' reverses the strike word, and 'In' places the trimmed write and the article within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is a union, so matters relating to it are matrimonial.

clue.text: Watery ditch is to the rear of sheep fold

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a leat is an open channel carrying water, as to a mill

explanation.surface: A water channel runs behind a sheep fold on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like a pen for sheep, but it is a folded crease in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressed crease or tuck in fabric, as in a skirt, is a fold.

clue.text: Squashes impulse in bed, getting ready to turn over

indicators.note: in puts the impulse word within the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
an urge is a sudden impulse

indicators.note: turning over means reading backwards

parts.note: set, as in 'ready, steady, go'

explanation.surface: Someone tossing and turning in bed, gripped by an impulse to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squashes' looks like a verb but is a plural noun: vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Zucchini are summer squashes, so these vegetables are examples of the plant family.

clue.text: Old twitcher's first to capture small, colourful bird

indicators.note: the pair of initials captures the small letter between them
the first letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: rich, as in deep, vivid colours

explanation.surface: An elderly birdwatcher's first sighting of a small, brightly coloured bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A twitcher is a keen birdwatcher, a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest living species of flightless bird, native to Africa.

clue.text: Criminal with affliction held up mature student

parts.note: an ill is a misfortune or ailment

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means reversed upwards

parts.note: to age is to mature
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A criminal with an illness robbed an older student at gunpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' suggests a robbery, but it reverses AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Against the law, as a criminal act is: an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Boxing ring is where, regularly, you'll get boisterous behaviour

indicators.note: boxing means putting a box around something, enclosing it
regularly takes every other letter

parts.note: a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A boxing ring is a place for rowdy goings-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing ring' looks like one phrase, but 'Boxing' is the container signal and 'ring' is the piece boxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy, exuberant fun and celebration, as in 'making whoopee', is boisterous behaviour.

clue.text: Economical? Yep, new Nissan's 50% smaller — that's revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned about, rearranged
half as big means only the first half of the car's name is kept

explanation.surface: A carmaker shrinks its Nissan by half, claiming a revolution in economy.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of NISSAN is NIS; 'that's revolutionary' shuffles YEP, NEW and NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful about small sums of money, thrifty; the question mark hints it is often 'and pound-foolish'.

clue.text: Right-armer's beginning to develop spin

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to evolve is to develop gradually

explanation.surface: A right-arm bowler in cricket starting to develop a spin delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: A right-armer is a cricket bowler who bowls with the right arm.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn around an axis is to spin: a direct synonym.

clue.text: At first, even critics lacked objectivity, given unusually explicit verse

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.words: even critics lacked objectivity, given unusually explicit

explanation.surface: Reviewers lost their detachment over some unusually explicit poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pastoral poem, such as Virgil's, is a form of verse.

clue.text: Shoe drops into the middle of Worcestershire river

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the other
the two central letters of the long county name

parts.note: raindrops, so drops gives rain

explanation.surface: A shoe falls into a river in the heart of Worcestershire, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like a verb, but it gives RAIN. The middle of WORCESTERSHIRE is TE; with R that makes TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports shoe, the British name for a sneaker, is a kind of shoe.

clue.text: Guardian essentially loathes Republican with American support

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: The Guardian newspaper essentially loathes Republicans with American backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the British newspaper but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person holding property or affairs in trust for others acts as a guardian of them.

clue.text: Getting a load of money in gilt-edged stocks

indicators.note: stocks as a verb: the phrase stocks, or holds, the letters within it

explanation.surface: Making a pile of money from investing in safe government securities.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilt-edged stocks are British government bonds, but 'stocks' means 'holds' here.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a load of something is slang for looking hard at it, which is watching it closely.

clue.text: In turning up on time, one makes contribution

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned around

explanation.surface: By arriving on time, one does one's bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reads as arriving, but 'turning' reverses UP to PU.
explanation.definitionFit: What someone puts into a discussion or project is their share, their contribution.

clue.text: Washing one left around, possibly wet?

indicators.note: around turns the two letters round

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a pound'
un-dry, not dry, so possibly wet: a made-up word the question mark excuses

explanation.surface: Someone left the washing out and now it's probably wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes and linen that are being or need to be washed are called the washing.

clue.text: Policeman seizes stolen loincloth

indicators.note: the policeman's letters seize, grip around, the stolen word

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a British police rank
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: An officer confiscates a stolen garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A long cloth wrapped round the waist and legs, worn by Hindu men in India, is a loincloth.

clue.text: Bill's in bed — rising temperature

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: Bill is ill in bed with a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but means an amount owed.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice or bill is a sum owed; money owed to someone is a liability.

clue.text: Half of police force needs a shake-up — it's handled by strict superior

indicators.note: being handled means held within, so the strict word goes around the shuffled letters

parts.note: tight, as in tight discipline

indicators.note: shaking up rearranges the letters
half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: Half the police force needs reform, a job for a strict senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs a shake-up' rearranges half of police plus the force letter; 'it's handled by' then sets that inside the strict word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the highest class or quality, top-ranking, as in a premier division: superior.

clue.text: When one interrupts, one gets delayed

indicators.note: the one letter breaks into the middle of the word for when

parts.note: once, as in 'once you've finished'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Whenever someone interrupts, the speaker gets held up.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: plans put on ice are postponed or shelved, so delayed.

clue.text: One of many paving blocks laid at end of street

parts.note: set, as in placed or laid down

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Paving stones being laid at the end of a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A squared granite block used in paving cobbled streets has this specific name.

clue.text: Charitable fellow with a small amount of money has been around previously

indicators.note: previously says this piece comes before the rest
around means the letters are turned about, rearranged

parts.note: has been gives BEEN, the past participle
a means one, and I is the Roman numeral for one
a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: A generous man with little money has been charitable before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the letters of 'has been'; 'previously' puts them in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing good and giving generously, as a benefactor does: a formal synonym for charitable.
